q: THWN stands for:
n: THWN = Thermoplastic, Heat- and Water (moisture)-resistant, Nylon-coated. Source: UL 83; Philippine Electrical Code.

q: Why do THHN and THWN wires have a nylon jacket?
n: The nylon jacket gives extra mechanical protection: it resists abrasion and cuts when wires are pulled through conduit, and also resists oils. Source: UL 83; wire manufacturer literature (Phelps Dodge).

q: What color is a ground wire in residential wiring?
n: Grounding conductors are green, green with yellow stripes, or bare copper. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (identification of grounding conductors).

q: What is conduit for?
n: Conduit is a raceway that encloses and protects wiring from physical damage and moisture. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (raceways).

q: What nominal voltage and frequency are used in the Philippines?
n: The Philippines uses 230 V nominal (often called 220 V) at 60 Hz. Source: Philippine Grid Code; Meralco service standards.

q: Which is a brand of electrical wire?
n: Phelps Dodge Philippines is a leading maker of electrical wire and cable. Panasonic, Omni and Schneider are other device brands. Source: Phelps Dodge Philippines company website.

q: Which of the following is considered the most expensive brand of circuit breakers?
n: Schneider Electric is a premium international brand and the most expensive of the choices. Koten and similar brands are economy lines. Source: Philippine electrical supplier price lists.

q: Which of the following is a cheaper brand of circuit breakers?
n: Koten is a budget circuit breaker brand sold in Philippine hardware stores. Panasonic, Schneider and ABB are premium brands. Source: Philippine electrical supplier price lists.

q: What is the typical power consumption (in watts per hour) of an air conditioner?
n: A typical 1–1.5 HP room air conditioner draws about 1,000–2,000 W while running. Source: DOE (Philippines) appliance energy labels; Meralco appliance wattage guide.

q: What is the typical power consumption (in watts per hour) of a water heater?
n: Electric water heaters typically draw about 3,000–4,000 W or more, among the highest household loads. Source: Meralco appliance wattage guide.

q: What is the typical power consumption (in watts per hour) of a blender?
n: Household blenders typically draw about 500–1,000 W. Short, intermittent use keeps a blender's actual energy consumption low despite its high momentary power draw. Source: Meralco appliance wattage guide.

q: What is the typical power consumption (in watts per hour) of an electric fan?
n: A standard electric fan draws on the order of 50–100 W, so 100 W is the matching value. Source: Meralco appliance wattage guide.

q: What is the typical power consumption (in watts per hour) of a portable fan?
n: Small portable fans draw about 10–100 W. This makes fans one of the most energy-efficient ways to improve comfort, far below an air conditioner's draw. Source: Meralco appliance wattage guide.

q: Which fixture is used to light wide areas for safety purposes?
n: Figure B, the wide panel light, gives broad, even illumination over large areas, as safety lighting needs. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Which fixture is usually installed behind walls or ceilings?
n: Figure D is a recessed fixture, installed in the cavity behind ceilings or walls so only its trim shows. Source: IES Lighting Handbook; luminaire manufacturer literature.

q: Which fixture is NOT typically required in working areas?
n: Figure C, a gooseneck accent lamp, is decorative and not required for general working areas, which need uniform task and ambient lighting. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Which fixture is used for general lighting purposes?
n: Figure A, the ceiling-mounted fixture, provides general (ambient) lighting. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Which fixture requires compliance with code?
n: Figure E is a life-safety fixture (emergency or exit lighting), whose installation must comply with code requirements. Source: RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019 (emergency lighting); Philippine Electrical Code.

q: Which lighting fixture is required on buildings according to the Code?
n: Figure C is an exit sign or emergency light, which the Fire Code and Building Code require on buildings. Source: RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019 (exit marking and emergency lighting); NBC IRR.

q: Which lighting fixture has a built-in battery?
n: Figure A has a built-in battery (an emergency driver module) that keeps the lamp lit during an outage. Source: Luminaire manufacturer literature; NFPA 101 Sec. 7.9.

q: Figure A is used for LED lighting and is called a:
n: An LED driver converts AC mains to the regulated DC current LEDs need. Ballasts are for fluorescent and HID lamps. Source: IES Lighting Handbook; IEC 61347 (lamp controlgear).

q: Figure B is typically specified as:
n: Figure B is an in-ground (well) light, specified for exterior ground lighting such as uplighting facades, trees and paths. Source: Luminaire manufacturer literature.

q: Figure C is a type of:
n: Figure C is an LED lamp. LED lamps give far more lumens per watt and a much longer life than incandescent or fluorescent lamps. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Which figure or figures represent energy-saving lighting?
n: The LED (C) and compact fluorescent (D) lamps are the energy-saving types, using far less power than incandescent or halogen for the same light. Source: DOE (Philippines) lighting efficiency standards; IES Lighting Handbook.

q: What component is necessary for the Figure D lamp to operate?
n: A compact fluorescent lamp (Figure D) needs a ballast, here an electronic ballast, to start it and regulate current. Source: IES Lighting Handbook; IEC 61347.

q: What is the primary purpose of image A, and in what types of locations is it most commonly used?
o: To connect water supply systems in industrial areas
To regulate voltage levels in a power grid
To power electrical devices in residential and commercial spaces
To measure electrical current in circuits
n: Image A is a wall receptacle (convenience outlet) that powers electrical devices in residential and commercial spaces. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (receptacles).

q: What advantage does image B provide compared to traditional wall outlets?
o: Is easier to install on concrete walls
Allows access to power in open floor areas while remaining flush when not in use
Provides higher voltage for heavy equipment
Offers surge protection for all devices
n: A pop-up floor outlet (image B) gives power in open floor areas away from walls and stays flush with the floor when closed. Source: Wiring device manufacturer literature.

q: Why is image C important for an outdoor electrical outlet?
o: It keeps moisture and debris out of the outlet, reducing electrical hazards
It increases current flow in wet areas
It lets devices run in high temperatures
It improves signal transmission for wireless devices
n: A weatherproof cover (image C) keeps rain, moisture and debris out of an outdoor outlet, reducing shock and short-circuit hazards. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (receptacles in wet locations); NEMA 250.

q: What safety function does image D serve, and where is it typically required?
o: It detects ground faults and cuts power to prevent shock; used in bathrooms and kitchens
It prevents circuit overloads in lighting systems
It controls voltage spikes; used in computer rooms
It measures current in industrial machinery
n: A GFCI (image D) detects ground-fault leakage and cuts power to prevent shock. It is required in bathrooms, kitchens and outdoors. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (GFCI protection); UL 943.

q: How does image E ensure a secure electrical connection between conductors?
o: It welds the wires with heat
It holds wires together with magnets
It crimps the wires by hydraulic pressure
It twists and holds the wires mechanically
n: A twist-on wire connector (image E) twists the conductors together and holds them mechanically with an internal spring, insulating the splice. Source: UL 486C (splicing wire connectors).

q: What lighting device, shown in Figure A and required by the building code, is typically used as an emergency source during power outages?
n: Figure A is a twin-head emergency light, which switches on automatically from its battery during a power outage, as the building and fire codes require. Source: RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019 (emergency lighting); NFPA 101 Sec. 7.9.

q: Which lighting fixture in Figure B is least commonly used in office spaces due to its exposed and decorative nature?
n: Exposed decorative LED strip lights (Figure B) are least used in offices, which favor troffers, panels and pendants for uniform, glare-controlled light. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (office lighting).

q: What lighting fixture in Figure C is typically used for high ceilings, such as those around 8 meters tall?
n: A high-bay pendant (Figure C) is hung from high ceilings, around 6–12 m, with optics that throw light down to the floor. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (industrial lighting).

q: Which lighting fixture in Figure D is suitable for exterior use due to its strong and focused illumination?
n: A floodlight (Figure D) gives strong, focused illumination for exteriors, facades and grounds. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (floodlighting).

q: Which lighting fixture in Figure E is most appropriate for illuminating wide areas in interior applications?
n: Recessed spotlights (Figure E), set in a regular grid, light wide interior areas evenly with no fixtures projecting below the ceiling. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: A factory-approved, fully assembled metal enclosure with fittings that contains bare conductors supported by insulators and is intended for use as a feeder.
n: A busway (bus bars) is a factory-assembled metal enclosure containing bare or insulated conductors on insulators, used as a feeder for large currents. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (busways).

q: From the service entrance to the feeder line and down to the branch line, where does the branch line terminate?
n: A branch circuit runs from the final overcurrent device at the panel and terminates at the outlets (receptacles and lighting points) it serves, not at a panel, breaker or meter. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (definition of branch circuit).

q: What box holds wire splices and is meant to be concealed and tamper-resistant?
n: A junction box encloses wire splices and taps. It must stay accessible but is closed with a cover so it is concealed and tamper-resistant. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (boxes).

q: What shape is a typical junction box for ceiling outlets?
n: Ceiling lighting outlets use octagonal junction boxes, which take fixture mounting straps and several conduit entries. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (outlet boxes); wiring device catalogs.

q: Which of these is NOT a protective electrical device?
n: CATV is cable television, a signal service. UPS units, voltage regulators and surge protectors protect equipment from power problems. Source: Philippine Electrical Code; IEC 62040 (UPS).
